title: Russian drone strike on Ukrainian park kills six, including two children
text: Russian forces used a drone to strike the central park in Nova Vodolaha, a town in Ukraine’s Kharkiv region, said Ivan Vyhivskyi, head of Ukraine’s Interior Ministry. Six people were killed: a man, three women, and two girls. One girl was 11, and the other was just over a year old, said Oleh Syniehubov, head of the Kharkiv regional military administration. Another 15 people were wounded, including seven children, he said. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the younger girl was named Angelina. Her mother, Inna, also died. Zelensky said a Shahed drone struck the park. title: What will Russia and the world look like in 2038? For Meduza’s 12th anniversary, we asked 12 people to share their hopes and predictions.
text: stories What will Russia and the world look like in 2038? For Meduza’s 12th anniversary, we asked 12 people to share their hopes and predictions. October 19, 2026, 5:58 pm Source: Meduza Meduza is 12! When we were just starting out in 2014, the world was a very different place — no COVID, no President Trump, no mass exodus of Russians. Russia’s war against Ukraine had already begun, though, and of course there was Putin (who had been in power long before that). What will the world and Russia be like in 12 years? And what would you like them to be like? We put these questions to 12 people we trust. Galina Timchenko, Meduza co-founder and publisher The honest answer to this question sounds pretty harsh, but what can you do: “I don’t know.” No, it’s worse than that: “Nobody knows.” There are too many variables, too many forks in the road. We’re still managing a precarious balancing act, but the risk of tumbling into catastrophe is greater than ever. Some things are obvious, like the AI “big bang”; others are less so, like the “rightward turn” in many countries. Making predictions is a thankless business. text: Енергостійкість громади починається з вірної тактики та продуманих рішень. Броварська міська територіальна громада витримала всі виклики минулої зими. І зараз, враховуючи досвід тотальних блекаутів, організовано та виважено підходить до нового опалювального сезону. В умовах війни енергостійкість — це не лише тепло в оселях, а й здатність громади працювати та забезпечувати життєво важливі послуги за будь-яких обставин. Впровадження енергозберігаючих технологій, встановлення альтернативних джерел енергії, забезпечення об’єктів критичної та соціальної інфраструктури необхідним автономним обладнанням - все це дозволяє громаді бути готовою до складних викликів сьогодення. Працюємо сьогодні, щоб завтра упевнено пройти зиму, оперативно реагуючи на поточні потреби. Стійкість громади починається з конкретних рішень і спільної відповідальності!

text: Говорив із Папою Римським Левом XIV і побажав Його Святості повного та швидкого відновлення після операції. Ми вдячні за те, що навіть у цей непростий особистий період Його Святість пам’ятає про Україну та молиться за наших людей. Детально розповів про ситуацію з російською ескалацією, постійні удари Росії по українських містах і громадах. Говорили й про гуманітарну катастрофу в тимчасово окупованих Олешках. Працюємо над тим, щоб допомогти нашим людям там. Готуємо рішення. Його Святість поінформував про контакти з російською стороною із цього приводу. Звісно, говорили також про всі безпекові виклики та загрози, які зараз є, зокрема періодичну відсутність попереджень від партнерів про російські балістичні атаки, що сталося вже тричі за останній час. Дякую Його Святості за підтримку та всі зусилля заради досягнення гідного миру.

text: Зустрівся в Києві з командою американської оборонної компанії Lockheed Martin, яка допомагає нам зберігати життя. Саме її системи Patriot і літаки F-16 відіграють важливу роль у захисті від російської балістики та реактивних «шахедів». І з обома напрямами зараз непросто. Обговорили, як можемо розширити та збільшити постачання. Зараз компанія нарощує виробництво перехоплювачів балістики. Розраховуємо, що частину з них зможемо закупити, щоб захистити більше життів. Також намагаємося зробити все, щоб обслуговування та ремонт F-16 відбувалися в Україні. Дякую за зустріч. Важливо, що Lockheed Martin присутня в Україні. text: Жахливий російський удар на Харківщині. «Шахед» ударив фактично просто по людях – по парку поблизу звичайного кафе. Абсолютне звірство. Шість людей загинули, і серед них діти. Дівчинка вбита у візочку. Її звали Ангеліна, їй було трохи більше року, вона народилась у серпні 2025 року… Її маму звали Інна, вона померла у лікарні… Іншій убитій дівчинці було 11 років. Мої співчуття рідним та близьким. Ще 14 людей поранені, і серед них ще шестеро дітей. Я вдячний усім, хто підтримує Україну у таких умовах і допомагає нам збивати «шахеди», збивати ракети, зупиняти російські штурми. Це страшні фото, але за ними – зламані життя і правда про цю війну. Потрібен захист життя. Потрібна ППО для України. Не можна думати про гроші з Росією, поки вона продовжує свою тупу війну. Ми просимо НЕ знімати санкції з Росії, поки вбивства не припинились. Ми просимо Америку бути сильною, просимо застосувати закон Ліндсі Грема. Ми просимо Європу продовжувати підтримку. Ми просимо робити все можливе, щоб мир настав і щоб безпека була гарантована. Україна хоче миру. Саме Росія увесь цей час наполягає на продовженні вбивств. Світ має достатню силу, щоб зупинити війну. Треба цією силою нарешті скористатись – проти

title: French authorities announce partial curfews as PM blames ‘ultra-left’ for exploiting protests – Europe live
text: 16.34 EDT The day so far Partial curfews have been issued for a number of French cities, including parts of Paris , after the government admitted police had “lost control” during violent weekend protests around the country. An overnight curfew will come into effect from 11pm until 6am local time, for Place ​de la Republique ⁠and the streets around ⁠Les Halles ​in Paris. Authorities earlier issued the country’s first curfew the northern city of Lille and surrounding cities of Douai, Wattignies and Denain. Curfews were also announced in the southern cities of Nice (specifically for minors) and central Lyon, while Marseille, earlier announced independently that it had banned all gatherings and demonstrations on Monday. It came after France’s PM, Sébastien Lecornu, said after an emergency cabinet meeting that he was “fully resolved to restore public order” and had called for “local and partial” curfews if needed. There was “no question” of imposing a full curfew on entire cities, he said. Lecornu told reporters that if declaring a state of emergency was deemed necessary “we could do so”, but ⁠added that at this stage partial curfews seemed “more appropriate”. title: Ukrainians dying because US restricting intelligence sharing, Zelensky adviser tells BBC
text: Ukrainians dying because US restricting intelligence sharing, Zelensky adviser tells BBC Image source, Naomi-Scherbel Ball/BBC Image caption, Serhii Beskrestnov said "people have already died" due to lack of warnings about incoming missile attacks By Dan Johnson Ukraine correspondent in Kyiv Published 19 October 2026 Ukrainians have died because Kyiv is still not receiving reliable US warnings of incoming Russian attacks, according to a key adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky. Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov told the BBC that lives had been lost because there had not been time to warn citizens about ballistic missile strikes, saying: "It's dangerous... I think it's really very bad... People [have] already died." The adviser also said restrictions to Ukraine's use of the Starlink internet network were ongoing. The White House said there had been no changes to intelligence sharing with Ukraine. Lavrov will meet with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian before holding “confidential and thorough” talks with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, according to a Russian Foreign Ministry statement. “Discussions will cover the situation in the Persian Gulf and ways to resolve the acute international crisis triggered by the unlawful U.S. and Israeli aggression against Iran,” the ministry said. title: Putin Approves Major Government Cabinet Reshuffle
text: Putin Approves Major Government Cabinet Reshuffle Oct. 19, 2026 Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov. The proposed personnel changes would replace nearly half of Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin’s deputy prime ministers, according to independent journalist Farida Rustamova. Rustamova said Dmitry Grigorenko’s removal from the post of chief of government staff was unexpected given his role as Mishustin’s “right-hand man” and his position being among “the most important in the government.” Mishustin’s spokesman later said Grigorenko himself had requested to be transferred to another post. Mishustin nominated First Deputy Finance Minister Irina Okladnikova to replace Grigorenko. If lawmakers approve her candidacy, she will become the first woman to ever hold the position of chief of government staff. title: Watch: Russian saboteur working for Ukraine shares reconnaissance videos
text: Watch: Russian saboteur working for Ukraine shares reconnaissance videos Watch: Russian saboteur working for Ukraine shares reconnaissance videos Close A Russian man secretly working for Ukraine's intelligence services has shared videos of surveillance work he says he has done for Kyiv inside Russia. title: Spain floods kill four as torrential rain inundates eastern regions
text: Torrential rain battered eastern Spain on Monday, killing at least four people in recent days as floodwaters swept away cars, submerged roads and stranded residents. Emergency crews carried out more than 400 rescues in Valencia, where rainfall reached 700 litres per square metre in 24 hours in some areas.

text: Ukrainian ⁠Foreign Minister ​Andrii Sybiha said on ​Monday that a summit between Russia, China ​and the ‌US would ⁠encourage President Vladimir Putin ‌to prolong the war. title: From Banking to Taxis, Ukraine’s Data Center Strikes Disrupt Everyday Life in Russia
text: From Banking to Taxis, Ukraine’s Data Center Strikes Disrupt Everyday Life in Russia By Moscow Times Reporter Oct. 19, 2026 A man walks past the Yandex office in Moscow. REUTERS / Anastasia Barashkova Andrei, a 39-year-old journalist from Moscow, looks at the notification on his smartphone and laughs. “Damn! I can’t log into my Yandex Pay account, but they’re still charging me for a Yandex Music subscription that doesn’t even work,” he says. When he tried to log in, the app displayed a message that said “Something went wrong” and asked him to try again later. “It’s a good thing I use another bank’s card for most of my payments,” he says. Yandex Pay is one of dozens of services whose operations have been disrupted by Ukrainian strikes on Russian data centers this month. For many Russians, these outages have mostly meant temporary inconveniences and changes to their routines. But in a year that has already seen widespread fuel shortages , airport closures and e-commerce disruptions due to the war, they are the latest way in which the Kremlin’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine has seeped into everyday life. text: Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line Close The Ukrainian military has released footage of what it says is the world's first drone airlift of a wounded soldier from the front line. The 92nd Assault Brigade said a ground rescue mission was not possible as the wounded serviceman was surrounded by landmines and there was high Russian drone activity in the area. It says a "heavy" hexacopter, piloted by a remote operator, was able to maintain stability during the "very difficult" operation. BBC Verify has confirmed the identity of the army personnel involved in the video, and found no signs of AI generation or manipulation. title: Kursk Becomes First Region to Appoint Ukraine War Veterans’ Rights Ombudsman
text: Kursk Becomes First Region to Appoint Ukraine War Veterans’ Rights Ombudsman Oct. 19, 2026 Maxim Kalutskikh. kurskcity.ru The southwestern Kursk region has become the first in Russia to appoint an ombudsman tasked with ensuring the rights of veterans who fought in the war against Ukraine, Governor Alexander Khinshtein announced Monday. “Essentially, we’re the first region where such a position is being introduced on a systematic basis,” Khinshtein said during a weekly regional government meeting. title: FM Lavrov Arrives in Tehran for Talks With Iranian Leadership
text: FM Lavrov Arrives in Tehran for Talks With Iranian Leadership Oct. 19, 2026 Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov. Russian Foreign Ministry Press Service Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov arrived in Tehran on Monday to hold a series of meetings with top Iranian officials as Moscow seeks to position itself as a mediator in the war between Iran and the United States. Lavrov will meet with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian before holding “confidential and thorough” talks with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, according to a Russian Foreign Ministry statement. “Discussions will cover the situation in the Persian Gulf and ways to resolve the acute international crisis triggered by the unlawful U.S. and Israeli aggression against Iran,” the ministry said. The bilateral agenda will also focus on energy, transport and economic projects, it added. Russia and Iran signed a strategic partnership agreement in 2025 that includes provisions for countering shared threats. That pact stops short of mutual defense obligations, unlike the security agreement Russia has signed with North Korea. news Medvedev to Lead Russian Delegation at Iranian Supreme Leader’s Funeral Read more Moscow is one of Tehran

title: Putin Approves Major Government Cabinet Reshuffle
text: Putin Approves Major Government Cabinet Reshuffle Oct. 19, 2026 Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov. Sputnik / Grigory Sysoyev / Pool via REUTERS President Vladimir Putin on Monday approved a major reshuffle of top government officials, coming weeks after Russia held parliamentary elections that handed the ruling United Russia party its largest-ever majority. The proposed personnel changes would replace nearly half of Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin’s deputy prime ministers, according to independent journalist Farida Rustamova. Rustamova said Dmitry Grigorenko’s removal from the post of chief of government staff was unexpected given his role as Mishustin’s “right-hand man” and his position being among “the most important in the government.” Mishustin’s spokesman later said Grigorenko himself had requested to be transferred to another post. Mishustin nominated First Deputy Finance Minister Irina Okladnikova to replace Grigorenko. If lawmakers approve her candidacy, she will become the first woman to ever hold the position of chief of government staff. title: Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line
text: Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line Close The Ukrainian military has released footage of what it says is the world's first drone airlift of a wounded soldier from the front line. The 92nd Assault Brigade said a ground rescue mission was not possible as the wounded serviceman was surrounded by landmines and there was high Russian drone activity in the area. It says a "heavy" hexacopter, piloted by a remote operator, was able to maintain stability during the "very difficult" operation. BBC Verify has confirmed the identity of the army personnel involved in the video, and found no signs of AI generation or manipulation. text: From Banking to Taxis, Ukraine’s Data Center Strikes Disrupt Everyday Life in Russia By Moscow Times Reporter Oct. 19, 2026 A man walks past the Yandex office in Moscow. REUTERS / Anastasia Barashkova Andrei, a 39-year-old journalist from Moscow, looks at the notification on his smartphone and laughs. “Damn! I can’t log into my Yandex Pay account, but they’re still charging me for a Yandex Music subscription that doesn’t even work,” he says. When he tried to log in, the app displayed a message that said “Something went wrong” and asked him to try again later. “It’s a good thing I use another bank’s card for most of my payments,” he says. Yandex Pay is one of dozens of services whose operations have been disrupted by Ukrainian strikes on Russian data centers this month. For many Russians, these outages have mostly meant temporary inconveniences and changes to their routines. But in a year that has already seen widespread fuel shortages , airport closures and e-commerce disruptions due to the war, they are the latest way in which the Kremlin’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine has seeped into everyday life. text: Tennis star Svitolina says emotional toll of Ukraine war led to Monfils separation Image source, Reuters Image caption, Monfils and Svitolina played in the mixed doubles together at this year's US Open and reached the semi-finals By Jack Burgess Published 19 October 2026 Ukrainian tennis star Elina Svitolina has announced the end of her marriage with French former tennis player GaÃ«l Monfils, citing the emotional impact of the war in her country. The 32-year-old, who is ranked number six in the world, wrote in a heartfelt post on Instagram about the effect the conflict and "what the war has done to me inside". "This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share," she wrote, saying "I need to find my way back to myself". Svitolina said she felt she could not do that within her marriage. She said her husband Monfils, 40, "listened" and "respected what I need with a strength and grace I will never forget". "Some battles happen deep inside you, and no amount of love from someone else can win them for you," the four-time Grand Slam semi-finalist wrote. title: Ukrainians dying because US restricting intelligence sharing, Zelensky adviser tells BBC
text: Ukrainians dying because US restricting intelligence sharing, Zelensky adviser tells BBC Image source, Naomi-Scherbel Ball/BBC Image caption, Serhii Beskrestnov said "people have already died" due to lack of warnings about incoming missile attacks By Dan Johnson Ukraine correspondent in Kyiv Published 19 October 2026 Ukrainians have died because Kyiv is still not receiving reliable US warnings of incoming Russian attacks, according to a key adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky. Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov told the BBC that lives had been lost because there had not been time to warn citizens about ballistic missile strikes, saying: "It's dangerous... I think it's really very bad... People [have] already died." The adviser also said restrictions to Ukraine's use of the Starlink internet network were ongoing. The White House said there had been no changes to intelligence sharing with Ukraine. Ukraine first reported an interruption to US intelligence sharing last week , as a row with the Trump administrations over its controversial deal to import Russian oil sent relations to new lows. title: Watch: Russian saboteur working for Ukraine shares reconnaissance videos
text: Watch: Russian saboteur working for Ukraine shares reconnaissance videos Watch: Russian saboteur working for Ukraine shares reconnaissance videos Close A Russian man secretly working for Ukraine's intelligence services has shared videos of surveillance work he says he has done for Kyiv inside Russia. The man, who we are calling Ivan, claims to have played a role in Ukrainian drone attacks on strategic bombers and munitions factories on his home soil. He features in a BBC World Service documentary about the shadowy world of Russian saboteurs. Ivan was cautious about how much detail he shared, making it impossible to verify the activities he claims to have carried out. Mikhail Razvozhayev, the Russian-appointed governor of Sevastopol, said Monday that purchase limits in the port city had been officially lifted as of midnight as shipments of fuel began to stabilize. “We’ve removed the restrictions because the logistics situation with gasoline has practically stabilized,” the Interfax news agency quoted Razvozhayev as saying. He said Sevastopol had enough fuel to ensure its “smooth sale over a short-term period,” though he said some gas stations ran out of certain fuel grades by midday on Monday before being restocked later in the day. “Let’s hope the logistics situation will remain this way from now on,” Razvozhayev said. news Russian Firms Stand to Gain Most From Trump’s Diesel Deal, Analysts Say Read more Crimea began rationing fuel in May after Ukrainian drone strikes targeted mili

text: ‘The Suicidal Fall of Europe’: Russia Reacts to Riots in France By Ned Garvey Oct. 19, 2026 Civil unrest in Paris. title: Kursk Becomes First Region to Appoint Ukraine War Veterans’ Rights Ombudsman
text: Kursk Becomes First Region to Appoint Ukraine War Veterans’ Rights Ombudsman Oct. 19, 2026 Maxim Kalutskikh. kurskcity.ru The southwestern Kursk region has become the first in Russia to appoint an ombudsman tasked with ensuring the rights of veterans who fought in the war against Ukraine, Governor Alexander Khinshtein announced Monday. “Essentially, we’re the first region where such a position is being introduced on a systematic basis,” Khinshtein said during a weekly regional government meeting. Maxim Kalutskhikh, a retired army colonel born in the Kursk region, will fill the newly created post. Kalutskikh fought in Ukraine between 2022 and 2023 and currently serves as deputy chairman of the Kursk region’s veterans association. title: FM Lavrov Arrives in Tehran for Talks With Iranian Leadership
text: FM Lavrov Arrives in Tehran for Talks With Iranian Leadership Oct. 19, 2026 Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov. Russian Foreign Ministry Press Service Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov arrived in Tehran on Monday to hold a series of meetings with top Iranian officials as Moscow seeks to position itself as a mediator in the war between Iran and the United States. Lavrov will meet with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian before holding “confidential and thorough” talks with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, according to a Russian Foreign Ministry statement. “Discussions will cover the situation in the Persian Gulf and ways to resolve the acute international crisis triggered by the unlawful U.S. and Israeli aggression against Iran,” the ministry said. The bilateral agenda will also focus on energy, transport and economic projects, it added. Russia and Iran signed a strategic partnership agreement in 2025 that includes provisions for countering shared threats. That pact stops short of mutual defense obligations, unlike the security agreement Russia has signed with North Korea. news Medvedev to Lead Russian Delegation at Iranian Supreme Leader’s Funeral Read more Moscow is one of Tehran

title: Putin Approves Major Government Cabinet Reshuffle
text: Putin Approves Major Government Cabinet Reshuffle Oct. 19, 2026 Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov. Sputnik / Grigory Sysoyev / Pool via REUTERS President Vladimir Putin on Monday approved a major reshuffle of top government officials, coming weeks after Russia held parliamentary elections that handed the ruling United Russia party its largest-ever majority. The proposed personnel changes would replace nearly half of Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin’s deputy prime ministers, according to independent journalist Farida Rustamova. Rustamova said Dmitry Grigorenko’s removal from the post of chief of government staff was unexpected given his role as Mishustin’s “right-hand man” and his position being among “the most important in the government.” Mishustin’s spokesman later said Grigorenko himself had requested to be transferred to another post. Mishustin nominated First Deputy Finance Minister Irina Okladnikova to replace Grigorenko. If lawmakers approve her candidacy, she will become the first woman to ever hold the position of chief of government staff. title: From Banking to Taxis, Ukraine’s Data Center Strikes Disrupt Everyday Life in Russia
text: From Banking to Taxis, Ukraine’s Data Center Strikes Disrupt Everyday Life in Russia By Moscow Times Reporter Oct. 19, 2026 A man walks past the Yandex office in Moscow. REUTERS / Anastasia Barashkova Andrei, a 39-year-old journalist from Moscow, looks at the notification on his smartphone and laughs. “Damn! I can’t log into my Yandex Pay account, but they’re still charging me for a Yandex Music subscription that doesn’t even work,” he says. When he tried to log in, the app displayed a message that said “Something went wrong” and asked him to try again later. “It’s a good thing I use another bank’s card for most of my payments,” he says. Yandex Pay is one of dozens of services whose operations have been disrupted by Ukrainian strikes on Russian data centers this month. For many Russians, these outages have mostly meant temporary inconveniences and changes to their routines. But in a year that has already seen widespread fuel shortages , airport closures and e-commerce disruptions due to the war, they are the latest way in which the Kremlin’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine has seeped into everyday life. text: Tennis star Svitolina says emotional toll of Ukraine war led to Monfils separation Image source, Reuters Image caption, Monfils and Svitolina played in the mixed doubles together at this year's US Open and reached the semi-finals By Jack Burgess Published 19 October 2026 Ukrainian tennis star Elina Svitolina has announced the end of her marriage with French former tennis player GaÃ«l Monfils, citing the emotional impact of the war in her country. The 32-year-old, who is ranked number six in the world, wrote in a heartfelt post on Instagram about the effect the conflict and "what the war has done to me inside". "This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share," she wrote, saying "I need to find my way back to myself". Svitolina said she felt she could not do that within her marriage. title: Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line
text: Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line Close The Ukrainian military has released footage of what it says is the world's first drone airlift of a wounded soldier from the front line. The 92nd Assault Brigade said a ground rescue mission was not possible as the wounded serviceman was surrounded by landmines and there was high Russian drone activity in the area. It says a "heavy" hexacopter, piloted by a remote operator, was able to maintain stability during the "very difficult" operation. BBC Verify has confirmed the identity of the army personnel involved in the video, and found no signs of AI generation or manipulation. title: Watch: Russian saboteur working for Ukraine shares reconnaissance videos
text: Watch: Russian saboteur working for Ukraine shares reconnaissance videos Watch: Russian saboteur working for Ukraine shares reconnaissance videos Close A Russian man secretly working for Ukraine's intelligence services has shared videos of surveillance work he says he has done for Kyiv inside Russia. The man, who we are calling Ivan, claims to have played a role in Ukrainian drone attacks on strategic bombers and munitions factories on his home soil. He features in a BBC World Service documentary about the shadowy world of Russian saboteurs. Ivan was cautious about how much detail he shared, making it impossible to verify the activities he claims to have carried out. "Given that all three heads of state may potentially take part in the summit in China, the subject of such a hypothetical meeting was indeed raised," spokesman Dmitry Peskov said in response to a Wall Street Journal report about ongoing talks to end the war. "It was raised, but no specific proposals or agreements were discussed or put forward by anyone, either regarding the meeting itself or the possible agenda and substance of that meeting," Peskov added. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha criticised the idea of holding a meeting in China without Ukraine's input. "A trilateral meeting between the leaders of Ukraine, the U.S. and Russia could help end the war sooner. title: Kursk Becomes First Region to Appoint Ukraine War Veterans’ Rights Ombudsman
text: Kursk Becomes First Region to Appoint Ukraine War Veterans’ Rights Ombudsman Oct. 19, 2026 Maxim Kalutskikh. kurskcity.ru The southwestern Kursk region has become the first in Russia to appoint an ombudsman tasked with ensuring the rights of veterans who fought in the war against Ukraine, Governor Alexander Khinshtein announced Monday. “Essentially, we’re the first region where such a position is being introduced on a systematic basis,” Khinshtein said during a weekly regional government meeting. Maxim Kalutskhikh, a retired army colonel born in the Kursk region, will fill the newly created post. Kalutskikh fought in Ukraine between 2022 and 2023 and currently serves as deputy chairman of the Kursk region’s veterans association. He graduated from the Ryazan Guards Higher Airborne Command School and has also served in an elite unit within Russia’s FSB security service. title: FM Lavrov Arrives in Tehran for Talks With Iranian Leadership
text: FM Lavrov Arrives in Tehran for Talks With Iranian Leadership Oct. 19, 2026 Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov. Russian Foreign Ministry Press Service Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov arrived in Tehran on Monday to hold a series of meetings with top Iranian officials as Moscow seeks to position itself as a mediator in the war between Iran and the United States. Lavrov will meet with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian before holding “confidential and thorough” talks with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, according to a Russian Foreign Ministry statement. “Discussions will cover the situation in the Persian Gulf and ways to resolve the acute international crisis triggered by the unlawful U.S. and Israeli aggression against Iran,” the ministry said. The bilateral agenda will also focus on energy, transport and economic projects, it added. Russia and Iran signed a strategic partnership agreement in 2025 that includes provisions for countering shared threats. That pact stops short of mutual defense obligations, unlike the security agreement Russia has signed with North Korea. news Medvedev to Lead Russian Delegation at Iranian Supreme Leader’s Funeral Read more Moscow is one of Tehran

title: Putin Approves Major Government Cabinet Reshuffle
text: Putin Approves Major Government Cabinet Reshuffle Oct. 19, 2026 Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov. Sputnik / Grigory Sysoyev / Pool via REUTERS President Vladimir Putin on Monday approved a major reshuffle of top government officials, coming weeks after Russia held parliamentary elections that handed the ruling United Russia party its largest-ever majority. The proposed personnel changes would replace nearly half of Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin’s deputy prime ministers, according to independent journalist Farida Rustamova. Rustamova said Dmitry Grigorenko’s removal from the post of chief of government staff was unexpected given his role as Mishustin’s “right-hand man” and his position being among “the most important in the government.” Mishustin’s spokesman later said Grigorenko himself had requested to be transferred to another post. Mishustin nominated First Deputy Finance Minister Irina Okladnikova to replace Grigorenko. If lawmakers approve her candidacy, she will become the first woman to ever hold the position of chief of government staff. title: Russia and Ukraine Should Focus on Peace Talks, Rubio Says
text: Russia and Ukraine Should Focus on Peace Talks, Rubio Says Oct. 19, 2026 U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. REUTERS / Kylie Cooper / Pool Ukraine and Russia should focus on ending the war between them, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters during his visit to Uzbekistan on Monday. "We see nothing good coming from this war," Rubio said. "We see a lot of downside to it, including the very real risk of escalation and spread of this thing... into another country because of a failed sabotage attack, because of drones that are hit with electronic warfare and they wander into a neighboring country." Rubio landed in Samarkand on Sunday night to meet top officials of the C5+1 grouping, which brings together the United States and the post-Soviet states of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan. U.S. President Donald Trump hosted C5 leaders at the White House last November. title: Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line
text: Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line Close The Ukrainian military has released footage of what it says is the world's first drone airlift of a wounded soldier from the front line. The 92nd Assault Brigade said a ground rescue mission was not possible as the wounded serviceman was surrounded by landmines and there was high Russian drone activity in the area. It says a "heavy" hexacopter, piloted by a remote operator, was able to maintain stability during the "very difficult" operation. BBC Verify has confirmed the identity of the army personnel involved in the video, and found no signs of AI generation or manipulation. title: From Banking to Taxis, Ukraine’s Data Center Strikes Disrupt Everyday Life in Russia
text: From Banking to Taxis, Ukraine’s Data Center Strikes Disrupt Everyday Life in Russia By Moscow Times Reporter Oct. 19, 2026 A man walks past the Yandex office in Moscow. REUTERS / Anastasia Barashkova Andrei, a 39-year-old journalist from Moscow, looks at the notification on his smartphone and laughs. “Damn! I can’t log into my Yandex Pay account, but they’re still charging me for a Yandex Music subscription that doesn’t even work,” he says. When he tried to log in, the app displayed a message that said “Something went wrong” and asked him to try again later. “It’s a good thing I use another bank’s card for most of my payments,” he says. Yandex Pay is one of dozens of services whose operations have been disrupted by Ukrainian strikes on Russian data centers this month. For many Russians, these outages have mostly meant temporary inconveniences and changes to their routines. But in a year that has already seen widespread fuel shortages , airport closures and e-commerce disruptions due to the war, they are the latest way in which the Kremlin’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine has seeped into everyday life. title: Annexed Crimea Begins Lifting Fuel Rationing Measures After Months of Shortages
text: Annexed Crimea Begins Lifting Fuel Rationing Measures After Months of Shortages Oct. 19, 2026 Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency Kremlin-installed authorities in Crimea have begun lifting fuel rationing measures introduced months ago in response to shortages caused by Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries and supply routes leading to the annexed peninsula. Mikhail Razvozhayev, the Russian-appointed governor of Sevastopol, said Monday that purchase limits in the port city had been officially lifted as of midnight as shipments of fuel began to stabilize. “We’ve removed the restrictions because the logistics situation with gasoline has practically stabilized,” the Interfax news agency quoted Razvozhayev as saying. He said Sevastopol had enough fuel to ensure its “smooth sale over a short-term period,” though he said some gas stations ran out of certain fuel grades by midday on Monday before being restocked later in the day. “Let’s hope the logistics situation will remain this way from now on,” Razvozhayev said. news Russian Firms Stand to Gain Most From Trump’s Diesel Deal, Analysts Say Read more Crimea began rationing fuel in May after Ukrainian drone strikes targeted mili

title: ‘The Suicidal Fall of Europe’: Russia Reacts to Riots in France
text: ‘The Suicidal Fall of Europe’: Russia Reacts to Riots in France By Ned Garvey Oct. 19, 2026 Civil unrest in Paris. REUTERS / Abdul Saboor As France picks up the pieces from a weekend that saw violent riots amid wider mass protests over education and the cost of living, reactions in Russia have ranged from outright glee and xenophobia to more muted schadenfreude and patronizing finger-wagging toward its Western adversary. On Monday, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that Europe was facing a “major crisis.” “It’s hard to say whether [this] is a systemic or non-systemic crisis, but it’s clear that it’s a major crisis. These are disturbances that are, in fact, already bordering on chaos,” Peskov told reporters. “There is, of course, a clear sign of a crisis here, but, in any case, this is an internal matter for these countries.” He dismissed accusations that Russia was involved in the protests, saying: “No one anywhere takes such absurd accusations seriously anymore. title: Tennis star Svitolina says emotional toll of Ukraine war led to Monfils separation
text: Tennis star Svitolina says emotional toll of Ukraine war led to Monfils separation Image source, Reuters Image caption, Monfils and Svitolina played in the mixed doubles together at this year's US Open and reached the semi-finals By Jack Burgess Published 19 October 2026 Ukrainian tennis star Elina Svitolina has announced the end of her marriage with French former tennis player GaÃ«l Monfils, citing the emotional impact of the war in her country. The 32-year-old, who is ranked number six in the world, wrote in a heartfelt post on Instagram about the effect the conflict and "what the war has done to me inside". "This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share," she wrote, saying "I need to find my way back to myself". Svitolina said she felt she could not do that within her marriage. She said her husband Monfils, 40, "listened" and "respected what I need with a strength and grace I will never forget". "Some battles happen deep inside you, and no amount of love from someone else can win them for you," the four-time Grand Slam semi-finalist wrote. It was "the hardest thing I have ever had to tell the person I love", Svitolina said. "Everyone knows how much Ukraine means to m

title: Ukrainians dying because US restricting intelligence sharing, Zelensky adviser tells BBC
text: Ukrainians dying because US restricting intelligence sharing, Zelensky adviser tells BBC Image source, Naomi-Scherbel Ball/BBC Image caption, Serhii Beskrestnov said "people have already died" due to lack of warnings about incoming missile attacks By Dan Johnson Ukraine correspondent in Kyiv Published 19 October 2026 Ukrainians have died because Kyiv is still not receiving reliable US warnings of incoming Russian attacks, according to a key adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky. Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov told the BBC that lives had been lost because there had not been time to warn citizens about ballistic missile strikes, saying: "It's dangerous... I think it's really very bad... People [have] already died." The adviser also said restrictions to Ukraine's use of the Starlink internet network were ongoing. The White House said there had been no changes to intelligence sharing with Ukraine. Ukraine first reported an interruption to US intelligence sharing last week , as a row with the Trump administrations over its controversial deal to import Russian oil sent relations to new lows. title: Watch: Russian saboteur working for Ukraine shares reconnaissance videos
text: Watch: Russian saboteur working for Ukraine shares reconnaissance videos Watch: Russian saboteur working for Ukraine shares reconnaissance videos Close A Russian man secretly working for Ukraine's intelligence services has shared videos of surveillance work he says he has done for Kyiv inside Russia. The man, who we are calling Ivan, claims to have played a role in Ukrainian drone attacks on strategic bombers and munitions factories on his home soil. He features in a BBC World Service documentary about the shadowy world of Russian saboteurs. Ivan was cautious about how much detail he shared, making it impossible to verify the activities he claims to have carried out. title: FM Lavrov Arrives in Tehran for Talks With Iranian Leadership
text: FM Lavrov Arrives in Tehran for Talks With Iranian Leadership Oct. 19, 2026 Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov. Russian Foreign Ministry Press Service Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov arrived in Tehran on Monday to hold a series of meetings with top Iranian officials as Moscow seeks to position itself as a mediator in the war between Iran and the United States. Lavrov will meet with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian before holding “confidential and thorough” talks with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, according to a Russian Foreign Ministry statement. “Discussions will cover the situation in the Persian Gulf and ways to resolve the acute international crisis triggered by the unlawful U.S. and Israeli aggression against Iran,” the ministry said. The bilateral agenda will also focus on energy, transport and economic projects, it added. Russia and Iran signed a strategic partnership agreement in 2025 that includes provisions for countering shared threats. text: From Banking to Taxis, Ukraine’s Data Center Strikes Disrupt Everyday Life in Russia By Moscow Times Reporter Oct. 19, 2026 A man walks past the Yandex office in Moscow. I can’t log into my Yandex Pay account, but they’re still charging me for a Yandex Music subscription that doesn’t even work,” he says. When he tried to log in, the app displayed a message that said “Something went wrong” and asked him to try again later. “It’s a good thing I use another bank’s card for most of my payments,” he says. Yandex Pay is one of dozens of services whose operations have been disrupted by Ukrainian strikes on Russian data centers this month. title: Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line
text: Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line Close The Ukrainian military has released footage of what it says is the world's first drone airlift of a wounded soldier from the front line. The 92nd Assault Brigade said a ground rescue mission was not possible as the wounded serviceman was surrounded by landmines and there was high Russian drone activity in the area. It says a "heavy" hexacopter, piloted by a remote operator, was able to maintain stability during the "very difficult" operation. BBC Verify has confirmed the identity of the army personnel involved in the video, and found no signs of AI generation or manipulation.
